title: Secret Service Overtime Pay Extension Act
official_summary:
Secret Service Overtime Pay Extension Act

This bill extends through 2023 the exemption of U.S. Secret Service officers, employees, and agents who perform protective services from the limitation on premium pay otherwise applicable to federal employees.

The bill also requires progress reports on the agency's implementation of certain Government Accountability Office and U.S. Secret Service Protective Mission Panel recommendations.

summary.headline: This law extends through 2023 an exemption that lets Secret Service staff who do protective work receive premium pay above the normal federal limit, and requires progress reports on agency reforms.
summary.what_it_does: Federal employees normally have a cap on how much premium pay, such as overtime, they can receive. This law keeps Secret Service officers, employees, and agents who perform protective services outside that cap through 2023. It also requires reports on how the agency is carrying out certain recommendations from the Government Accountability Office and the Secret Service Protective Mission Panel.

who_it_affects.group: Secret Service officers, employees, and agents who perform protective services
who_it_affects.how: They remain exempt from the federal limit on premium pay through 2023, so they can receive overtime and other premium pay above that cap.

who_it_affects.group: U.S. Secret Service as an agency
who_it_affects.how: It must report on its progress in carrying out certain recommendations from the Government Accountability Office and the Secret Service Protective Mission Panel.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on December 30, 2020, and the pay exemption runs through 2023.
